title: A room full of handshakes
hook: Everyone at a party shakes everyone's hand once. How fast does that pile up?

knows: adding a run of numbers like 1 + 2 + ... + 9
doesNotKnow: why the number of pairs among n people is n × (n − 1) ÷ 2

misconception: n people shake hands n × n times, or n × (n − 1) times.
objective: The learner can explain that each of 10 people shakes 9 hands, giving 10 × 9 = 90, but every handshake was counted at both hands, so there are 45.

claims.text: When person k arrives they shake k − 1 hands, so 10 people make 1 + 2 + ... + 9 = 45 handshakes.
claims.source: Each newcomer pairs with everyone already present; sum 1..9 = 45 (recomputed in node). The stage draws one line per pair.

claims.text: Each of the 10 people has 9 lines, so 10 × 9 = 90 line ends; every handshake has two ends, so there are 90 ÷ 2 = 45.
claims.source: Double counting (handshake lemma): the degrees sum to twice the number of edges. 10 × 9 / 2 = 45 (node).

claims.text: 10 × 10 = 100 also counts people shaking their own hand.
claims.source: n × n counts every ordered pair (a, b) including a = b; removing the 10 self-pairs gives 90 ordered pairs, halved to 45.

recall.question: In a league of 6 teams, every team plays every other team once. How many games?
recall.why: Each team plays 5 games, 6 × 5 = 30, but each game was counted for both teams, so 30 ÷ 2 = 15.
